title: New school approved at 20 Woolner Trail
subtitle: Ward 10 councillor sworn in, bylaw penalty system expanded, heritage approvals, surplus city land for housing, dog designation appeal
overview: Council's first meeting of 2024 began with the swearing-in of Stephanie Stretch as the new Ward 10 councillor, filling the vacancy left late in 2023. Council also welcomed a new Chief of Staff for the Office of the Mayor and Council and heard that Kitchener has been certified a Better City for Pets.

The main decision was approval of the Official Plan and zoning changes for a Waterloo Catholic District School Board high school at 20 Woolner Trail {{vote:m2}}. Council had deferred the item twice over traffic and student safety. Nearby residents asked for another deferral, but council went ahead after staff, the school board and the Region agreed on speed and crossing measures.

Council expanded the Administrative Monetary Penalty System to cover many non-parking by-laws {{vote:m4}}. It approved heritage permit and designation steps for downtown and Eby and Victoria Street properties, and upheld dog designations with modified conditions {{vote:m1}}. Staff must also report by the end of Q2 2024 on surplus City-owned land, including surface parking lots, that could be used for housing {{vote:m9}}. A separate application at Benton and St. George streets was removed from the agenda because it has been appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the Official Plan amendment and approved the zoning by-law amendment for the Waterloo Catholic District School Board site, with the Official Plan amendment forwarded to the Region for approval.
Council expanded administrative monetary penalties to non-parking by-laws, approved a new screening and hearing officer by-law and amended about two dozen by-laws and six related policies.

decisions.item: Heritage permit, 149-151 Ontario St N and 21 Weber St W
decisions.detail: Council approved partial demolition with retained west and south facades and a new 27-storey mixed-use tower, subject to conditions on heritage plans and clearances.

decisions.item: Heritage designation of 33 Eby St S and 72 Victoria St S
decisions.detail: Council recognized the cultural heritage value of both properties and agreed to pursue designation under the Ontario Heritage Act.

As amended, staff must identify surplus or underused City-owned land, including surface parking lots, for housing and report options by the end of Q2 2024, then share the resolution with the Region and other municipalities.
Council confirmed the appeal committee's decisions on a potentially dangerous designation for one dog and a dangerous designation for another, both with modified conditions.

debate: Residents of the Woolner Trail neighbourhood asked for another deferral. They called the staff approach, which relies on measures being taken later if warranted, inadequate for student safety and traffic, and asked that commitments from the Region and school board be confirmed in writing first. They pointed to options being explored in Cambridge.

School board representatives and several councillors said the extra work had produced real changes: added entrances from Fairway Road, a student drop-off area, buses staged on school property, a multi-use trail, lower speed limits with automated enforcement, a crossing guard and further regional study of a pedestrian signal. Speakers acknowledged it was not perfect but said the school is needed and the delay should end.

On the land-for-housing motion, councillors said staff already had land inventory work under way. They supported surface parking lots as another tool, including possible temporary or modular housing, and wanted results shared with regional partners. A Habitat for Humanity presentation earlier in the evening asked for low- or no-cost land through transparent City processes.
The dog owner who delegated disputed the account of the incident, said the larger dog is gentle, and asked council to remove the designation for that dog and keep a muzzle order for the other.

In the information item on bid solicitations, a councillor asked about unspent fire apparatus funds. Staff said the budget is in US dollars, other items will draw on it, and any remainder stays in the fire equipment budget.
